summary: Overall risk HIGH (performance_risk=7). The change is small and additive, but it lands in the SessionStart hook every fleet seat's registration depends on, and it writes to an append-only table whose rows can never be deleted. Two defects are live-reproducible TODAY against the current fleet: (1) model-policy.cjs seatClassFor() collapses unknown-role to 'worker', and the live coordinator seat 3616c697 carries is_coordinator:true with NO metadata.role -- a naive wire emits a FALSE mismatch for a seat that is ON policy; (2) capture-session-id.cjs's time budget is already over-subscribed (worst case ~22s vs a 13500ms self-resolve / 15s registered timeout), so an unguarded added round trip degrades session registration fleet-wide. Proceed with the mitigations below encoded as PRD requirements.
justification: Assessed by reading scripts/hooks/capture-session-id.cjs in full (864 lines), lib/fleet/model-policy.cjs, lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs, lib/governance/emit-feedback.js, scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs, database/chairman-gated/20260907_feedback_immutability_trigger.sql, and the .claude/settings.json SessionStart registration; plus three LIVE measurements against production Supabase: the feedback append-only trigger state (a PATCH probe returned P0001 'feedback is append-only', so the trigger IS applied despite the file header reading @approved-by PENDING), the feedback column set, and the role/model metadata of all 10 active claude_sessions rows. Verdict is CONDITIONAL_PASS rather than PASS because HIGH risk requires a documented mitigation plan per the risk sub-agent blocking criteria, and because the false-positive defect is reproducible on the current fleet rather than hypothetical.
critical_issues: FALSE-POSITIVE ON ROLE SEATS, LIVE-REPRODUCIBLE. lib/fleet/model-policy.cjs seatClassFor() classifies any undefined/null/unrecognized role as 'worker'. Measured live: of the 4 role seats active now, the coordinator (3616c697) carries is_coordinator:true and NO metadata.role -- exactly the QF-20260906-473 shape -- and runs claude-fable-5-1, which IS its correct policy model. Naive wiring flags it as off-policy. Worse, at SessionStart the claude_sessions row for a FRESH session does not exist yet (upsertSessionRow's GET fails open to existingMetadata={}), so EVERY role seat's first SessionStart is role-unknown and would emit a false mismatch on every restart. This is the exact three-state collapse SD-LEO-INFRA-ROLE-BLIND-SESSION-001 FR-1 created lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs to prevent, and SessionStart was one of its three original defect sites.

HOOK TIME BUDGET IS ALREADY OVER-SUBSCRIBED. Registered timeout is 15s (.claude/settings.json) and the hook self-resolves at 13500ms. Existing worst path: tree_walk 6000ms + scan 3000ms + metadata GET 2000ms + 3 upsert attempts (0+3000, 500+3000, 1500+3000) is roughly 22s. Any added network round trip that can block the resolve makes a slow SessionStart slower for EVERY seat on EVERY startup/resume/clear/compact. This is the blast-radius vector, not a logic bug.

FEEDBACK ROWS ARE PERMANENT. Verified live, not inferred: public.feedback carries feedback_no_update / feedback_no_delete_trg / feedback_no_truncate_trg, all ENABLE ALWAYS (a PATCH probe returned P0001). INSERT is unaffected and works normally, but a wrong or noisy row can never be corrected or deleted -- only superseded by another row. A mis-scoped signal that fires on every compact would permanently pollute the harness-backlog surface.
warnings: SECOND WRITER TO A TABLE WITH A DECLARED CANONICAL WRITER. lib/governance/emit-feedback.js is marked @canonical-writer-for: feedback, but it is ESM and pulls @supabase/supabase-js, the audit-events emitter, the vision event bus, and buildMeasurementProvenance (which shells out to git) -- unusable from this dependency-free, latency-sensitive CJS hook. A direct PostgREST insert (mirroring upsertSessionRow's own pattern) is the right call, but it must be declared as a deliberate second writer in the code comment and must reproduce emitFeedback's dedup shape exactly: sha256 over date + description + dedup_key, stored at metadata.dedup_hash, with SELECT-then-skip. Note emitFeedback dedups by SKIPPING, never by UPDATEing occurrence_count -- that is precisely what keeps it compatible with the append-only trigger, and the hook must copy that property.

DEDUP IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL. SessionStart fires on startup, resume, clear and compact. An off-policy seat in a long session could emit dozens of rows per day into a table that cannot be purged. Date-salted dedup caps it at one row per seat per model-change per day.

DRY-RUN MUST BE HONORED. LEO_HOOK_DRY_RUN=1 already skips both upsertSessionRow's write and the session-tick spawn. SD-LEO-FIX-RELEASED-TEST-FIXTURE-001 documents what happens when one write path forgets: a dry-run test becomes a false witness by creating real rows while asserting none were written. The new write must sit behind the same guard.

buildSessionMetadata's NO-MODEL PATH IS PINNED. The function's own comment and tests/unit/capture-session-id-metadata-merge.test.js pin the no-model output to exactly {cc_pid, source}. The mismatch check must not add keys to the returned metadata object outside the existing if (model) block; keep the signal entirely out of buildSessionMetadata and do it at the call site in main().

FIRE-AND-FORGET WOULD BE KILLED MID-FLIGHT. main() resolves and the entrypoint calls drainAndExit(0), which destroys the undici dispatcher within 200ms and then process.exit()s. An unawaited fetch would be aborted non-deterministically. The write must be awaited with a tight timeout, not detached.

TWO READERS OF ONE POLICY MUST NOT DIVERGE. The dashboard count and the hook signal must derive from the SAME predicate, or the coordinator sees a number that disagrees with the rows. scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs:338 already SELECTs the full metadata column per session and merges only model/effort at line 362 -- the role fields join that same merge, so the count is zero extra query.
recommendations: M1 (closes critical #1) THREE-STATE ROLE GATE. require lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs (already CJS, already loaded defensively by the sibling SessionStart hook session-role-orient.cjs) and call verdictFromMetadata(existingMetadata) BEFORE checkModelMismatch. Signal only when the verdict is 'role' or 'worker'; on 'unknown' -- and on an absent or unfetchable claude_sessions row -- stay silent. Do NOT pass a bare role string into checkModelMismatch and trust its worker default. This mirrors checkModelMismatch's own posture that an absent observed model never trips.

M2 (closes critical #2) LAST-IN-LINE, SINGLE ATTEMPT, HARD DEADLINE. Insertion point: in main()'s stdin end handler, AFTER await upsertSessionRow(...) and after the session-tick spawn block, immediately before resolve(). At that point the env file, PID marker, session marker, /current pointer, stdout lines, the DB upsert and the tick daemon are ALL already complete -- nothing downstream can be gated by it. One attempt, no retry loop, AbortController at 1500ms or less, and a Promise.race against a hard deadline. Do not raise MAX_ATTEMPTS and do not extend the 13500ms self-resolve timer.

M3 FAIL-OPEN TRY/CATCH, NEVER RETHROW. Wrap the whole block in its own try/catch that swallows everything, matching the file's established pattern (resolveRepoRoot fails open to cwd, findLiveTickPid fails open to no-daemon, the marker block's bare catch Non-fatal, the metadata GET's fail-open catch, tier_rank's fail-open catch). Also guard the module require itself in try/catch the way session-role-orient.cjs lines 10-13 does, so a missing or broken lib/fleet/model-policy.cjs degrades to pre-change behavior instead of taking SessionStart down.
M4 KILL SWITCH + DRY-RUN. Honor LEO_MODEL_POLICY_SIGNAL=0 to disable the write entirely, and skip it under LEO_HOOK_DRY_RUN=1 exactly as upsertSessionRow and the tick spawn already do.

M5 (closes critical #3) DEDUP + BOUNDED CONTENT. Date-salted dedup_hash over (YYYY-MM-DD, session_id, observed family, expected family) at metadata.dedup_hash, with a SELECT-then-skip pre-check and no UPDATE anywhere -- append-only compatible by construction. Row shape: type=issue, category=harness_backlog, source_application=EHG_Engineer, source_type=manual_feedback, session_id set, severity bounded, title capped at 120 chars (emitFeedback's own cap). Content is machine-derived (session_id, role verdict, model ids) -- no secrets, no free text.

M6 MEASURE BEFORE YOU WRITE, AND SHIP IN TWO COMMITS. Before enabling the write, run a read-only script over live claude_sessions that prints which seats WOULD be flagged, and confirm every flag is a true positive. The equivalent read was run during this assessment: with the naive predicate, 45924f8d (worker on fable) is a genuine hit and 3616c697 (coordinator on fable) is a false positive -- roughly a 50% false-positive rate on the fleet as it stands. Land the hook wiring and the dashboard count as separately revertible commits (the same discipline SD-FDBK-ENH-SESSIONSTART-HOOK-CAPTURE-001 FR-5 used for its timer bump).

M7 TESTS. Extend tests/unit/hooks/capture-session-id.test.cjs with four cases: (a) a throw injected into the mismatch check still completes session registration; (b) role-unknown writes nothing; (c) is_coordinator:true on fable writes nothing; (d) a worker on fable writes exactly one row and a second SessionStart the same day writes none. The six existing capture-session-id test files are the regression net for the untouched paths and must all stay green.

M8 SCOPE. Estimated ~45 LOC in the hook plus ~15 LOC in the dashboard plus tests -- inside the 100 LOC target. Resist enlarging: do NOT refactor buildSessionMetadata, do NOT move the marker-location logic, do NOT touch the retry policy.

conditions.action: M1: gate the signal on lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs verdictFromMetadata -- signal only on verdict role or worker, never on unknown or an absent session row
M2: insert the call last in main(), after upsertSessionRow and the tick spawn, single attempt, AbortController 1500ms or less, no change to MAX_ATTEMPTS or the 13500ms self-resolve timer
M3: fail-open try/catch around both the require and the call; the block can never throw into SessionStart
M5: date-salted dedup_hash with SELECT-then-skip and no UPDATE -- the feedback append-only trigger is applied live and rows cannot be deleted
M4: LEO_MODEL_POLICY_SIGNAL=0 kill switch and LEO_HOOK_DRY_RUN=1 skip
M6: read-only live dry-run confirming zero false positives before the write is enabled; hook and dashboard land as separately revertible commits
M7: four new hook tests (throw-injection, unknown-role silence, coordinator silence, worker true-positive plus same-day dedup); six existing capture-session-id test files stay green

detailed_analysis.blast_radius: capture-session-id.cjs is the FIRST hook in the second SessionStart group (.claude/settings.json), ahead of session-register.cjs and session-role-orient.cjs. It writes CLAUDE_SESSION_ID to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE (every subsequent Bash tool call depends on it), the pid-keyed and session-keyed identity markers and the /current pointer (claim-validity-gate's three identity sources), the claude_sessions row (the row session-tick.cjs later PATCHes), and spawns the detached tick daemon. A throw or hang anywhere in main() before resolve() degrades or loses all of that for every seat. The mitigating fact is that the proposed insertion point is AFTER all of it: at that line the only remaining statement is resolve(), so an additive block there cannot gate anything that already happened.
detailed_analysis.existing_fail_safe_patterns_to_follow: The file has a consistent, well-established fail-open idiom worth copying verbatim rather than inventing: resolveRepoRoot() catches and returns cwd; findLiveTickPid() catches and returns null (documented as only ever SKIPS a spawn, never blocks one); the entire marker-write block ends in catch { // Non-fatal }; the metadata GET is wrapped in a fail-open catch; tier_rank re-derivation uses a fail-open catch that keeps whatever tier_rank was already stamped; the outermost JSON.parse is wrapped in catch { // Invalid JSON or other error -- do not block session start }; and the entrypoint is main().then(drainAndExit(0)).catch(drainAndExit(0)). Note the last one: even an unhandled rejection exits 0. That is a safety net, NOT a licence to skip the local catch -- a throw before resolve() would still skip everything after it.
detailed_analysis.safe_insertion_point: main(), stdin end handler, after the LEO_HOOK_DRY_RUN early return and after the try/catch that wraps the session-tick spawn -- i.e. the last statement before the handler's closing catch. Everything the hook exists to do is finished by that line. A second acceptable option, if the PRD prefers lower blast radius over co-location with the model stamp, is scripts/hooks/session-role-orient.cjs (3s timeout, runs third, already requires role-status-identity.cjs defensively and already resolves the role verdict). It would not need M1's plumbing at all. Co-location with the metadata.model stamp argues for capture-session-id.cjs; blast radius argues for session-role-orient.cjs. Either is defensible; do NOT put it inside buildSessionMetadata.
detailed_analysis.feedback_table_subtlety: Measured live, not read off the migration header: the append-only trio IS applied to public.feedback (a PATCH against a real row returned HTTP 400 / P0001 'feedback is append-only: row ... cannot be modified after insert'). Two consequences. (1) INSERT is completely unaffected -- there is no INSERT trigger and service_role holds the grant, so a plain PostgREST POST works. (2) Any dedup strategy that bumps occurrence_count or last_seen via UPDATE will throw. emitFeedback already dedups by SELECT-then-skip rather than by UPDATE, so copying its shape is both the canonical and the only trigger-compatible option. Separately: the migration file at database/chairman-gated/20260907_feedback_immutability_trigger.sql still reads @approved-by PENDING while the triggers are live -- the header is a ceremony marker, never apply state, so trust the probe.
detailed_analysis.live_fleet_measurement: 10 active claude_sessions rows at assessment time. Role seats: d7064121 (role=michael, non_fleet=true, fable), 49eabb23 (role=adam, non_fleet=true, claude-fable-5-1), d3430608 (role=solomon, non_fleet=true, claude-fable-5-1), 3616c697 (NO role key, is_coordinator=true, claude-fable-5-1). Worker or unlabelled: 689a1237 and 64728de4 (sonnet), a531d943 / 6acf5a48 / acf89031 (claude-opus-5 1m), 45924f8d (role absent, model=fable). Under the naive predicate the coordinator 3616c697 is a FALSE positive (fable is its correct policy model, reached via is_coordinator not via a role string) and 45924f8d is the genuine hit the SD exists to catch. Under M1's three-state gate the coordinator is correctly classified role (verdictFromMetadata returns ROLE on is_coordinator===true, per QF-20260906-473) and the worker still trips.
detailed_analysis.dashboard_surface: scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs is the live surface (3457 lines, npm run fleet:dashboard, referenced by /coordinator, the /adam belt-countdown duty and /execute); scripts/archive/one-time/fleet-dashboard.cjs is archived and must not be touched. The seats section at line 338 already SELECTs session_id plus the full metadata column for every active session and merges a fixed field list at lines 345-363 (model and effort come through there already). Adding role, is_coordinator and non_fleet to that same Object.assign and computing the off-policy count from the already-loaded rows costs zero additional queries and is purely additive to the render.
